ordered_diagnoses: Single Ventricle Defect with D-Transposition of the Great Arteries

facts.raw_span: single ventricle defect, double-outlet right ventricle with D-transposition of the great arteries, and an ostium secundum atrial septal defect with left superior vena cava
showed no signs of respiratory distress
became hemodynamically unstable and suffered a cardiorespiratory arrest requiring cardiac massage
clonic movements of the left upper limb and persistent sucking motions
a slight diffuse increase in cortical density predominantly in the right frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes and, to a lesser extent, in the left parietal and occipital lobes

showed no signs of respiratory distress
became hemodynamically unstable and suffered a cardiorespiratory arrest requiring cardiac massage
clonic movements of the left upper limb and persistent sucking motions
a slight diffuse increase in cortical density predominantly in the right frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes and, to a lesser extent, in the left parietal and occipital lobes

concepts.why: The patient's history of occasional cyanosis, low oxygen saturation, and cardiorespiratory arrest, followed by clonic movements and increased cortical density on head CT, are consistent with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.

The patient's development of clonic movements and increased cortical density on head CT after receiving nonionic iodinated contrast (Iopromide) during cardiac catheterization suggests contrast-induced encephalopathy.
The patient's clonic movements of the left upper limb and persistent sucking motions are consistent with a seizure disorder.
The patient's history of cardiorespiratory arrest and subsequent development of clonic movements and increased cortical density on head CT are consistent with cardiac arrest encephalopathy.

concepts.why: The patient's known complex congenital heart disease, including single ventricle defect, double-outlet right ventricle with D-transposition of the great arteries, and ostium secundum atrial septal defect, is consistent with this diagnosis.

rationales.F10: Cardiorespiratory arrest is a known risk factor for hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and cardiac arrest encephalopathy.
rationales.F11: Clonic movements and persistent sucking motions are indicative of seizure activity, which is a common manifestation of hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, contrast-induced encephalopathy, and seizure disorder.
rationales.F12: The slight diffuse increase in cortical density on the head CT is consistent with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and contrast-induced encephalopathy.
